newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BORO'S WAIT GOES ON AS LEICESTER SNATCH EQUALISER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BORO'S WAIT GOES ON AS LEICESTER SNATCH EQUALISER.

text.p: A Leicester equaliser three minutes from the end of extra-time forced a 1-1 draw in the English League Cup final on Sunday and deprived Middlesbrough of the first major trophy in their 121-year history.

Middlesbrough opened the scoring five minutes into extra time when Fabrizio Ravanelli lashed home a left-foot drive from eight metres just two minutes after missing a far easier chance when he fired straight at Leicester goalkeeper Kasey Keller.

Boro, who just about deserved to win a match which began at pedestrian pace but ended with a frenzy, were just over three minutes away from long-awaited glory and a place in next season's UEFA Cup when Leicester equalised.

A cross from substitute Mark Robins, a former team mate of Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson at Manchester United, was headed back across goal by Leicester skipper Steve Walsh. Emile Heskey rose above Gianluca Festa to head the ball against the bar for the second time in the match.

Unlike the first occasion when the ball bounced into touch, it rebounded back into play and after Leicester's Steve Claridge got a touch to start a defensive scramble, Heskey stabbed it over the line to make the final score 1-1.
The replay will take place at Hillsborough in Sheffield on April 16.

But the replay is a match Middlesbrough will feel they should have avoided. Ravanelli could have made the game safe for Boro in normal time but sunk to his knees in theatrical agony after watching his glancing header hit the post after 78 minutes.
He then missed a sitter two minutes into extra time just before finally scoring his 27th goal since his 7.0 million pounds ($11.2 million) move from Juventus last summer.

Leicester, who have lost all four F.A. Cup finals they have played at Wembley and who themselves were looking for their first major honour since winning the League Cup in 1964, had little of Middlesbrough's attacking verve.
But they largely nullified the impact Brazilian Juninho made on the game by man-marking him with Swedish defender Pontus Kaamark.
The Leicester defender did a thorough job but could do nothing to stop Juninho's mazy run which helped create Ravanelli's goal.

Middlesbrough's other Brazilian Emerson was involved in most of their most dangerous build-ups, but despite the tense finale the game was generally disappointing, especially during the opening 45 minutes during which neither team had a shot on target.
Both teams played attractive football in midfield but Heskey and Claridge had a frustrating afternoon in the Leicester attack producing little of real venom.

Leicester manager Martin O'Neill said afterwards: "I am delighted we came through that. Middlesbrough had the chance to open us up after taking the lead and could have gone on to score a second. We left ourselves exposed but Heskey did brilliantly to score."
He also revealed he only told Kaamark of his role 80 minutes before the match.

"He was delighted to be in the team until I told him before kick-off that his job was to man-mark Juninho," O'Neill said. "The smile just disappeared from his face. I thought he did brilliantly for us."
Robson said the mood in his dressing room was despondent afterwards.

"It's disappointing when you've been quite dominant in the game and have had good chances not to go on and win. On another day Ravanelli could have had a hat-trick, he's always in there and with a bit of luck could have scored three."
The match went ahead without reports of breaches of security following the chaos caused by coded bomb warnings at the Grand National on Saturday.
The only incidents stewards had to deal with were three male streakers on the pitch.
